cards.explanation: The answer is that they go into exile. The people of Jerusalem went into exile in the fifth month of the eleventh year of Zedekiah, the king of Judah named last in the list (Jeremiah 1:3). That's where the stretch of Jeremiah's messages ends. The word of the LORD kept coming to him through the days of Jehoiakim and on until that point.
The answer is womb. The LORD says, "Before I formed you in the womb I knew you…" (Jeremiah 1:5). Think about that, friends. Before Jeremiah had a first day, the LORD already knew him.

The answer is prophet. The LORD says, "…before you were born I set you apart and appointed you as a prophet to the nations." So the appointing came before Jeremiah's birth. His job was picked before he could pick anything.

The answer is speak. Jeremiah says, "I surely do not know how to speak, for I am only a child!" The LORD has just appointed him as a prophet to the nations. I think speaking was exactly what was on his mind.
The answer is False. The LORD says, "…to everyone I send you, you must go, and all that I command you, you must speak." He says everyone and all. Jeremiah doesn't get to cross anything off.

The answer is deliver. The LORD says, "Do not be afraid of them, for I am with you to deliver you…" Notice the reason is not that the people are friendly. The reason is that the LORD is with Jeremiah.
The answer is His words. The LORD says, "Behold, I have put My words in your mouth." The mouth Jeremiah was worried about now has the LORD's words in it. I'd say that settles the speaking question.
The answer is True. The list ends with "…to build and plant." So the job has four hard verbs up front, then two more at the end. The LORD's list doesn't stop at tearing down.
The answer is True. The LORD says, "You have observed correctly…" Jeremiah saw a branch of an almond tree, and he saw it right. I'd bet he breathed out after that one.

The answer is His word, to make it happen. The LORD says, "…I am watching over My word to accomplish it." So His word is what He keeps His eye on. He says this right after Jeremiah tells Him he sees a branch of an almond tree (Jeremiah 1:11).
The answer is disaster. The LORD says, "Disaster from the north will be poured out on all who live in the land." That's what the tilting pot was showing. It's a heavy word.

The answer is thrones. The LORD says the kings "…will come and set up their thrones at the entrance of the gates of Jerusalem." Thrones is the word the verse picks. The verse goes on to say they will attack all her surrounding walls and all the other cities of Judah.

The answer is that they left Him for other gods. The LORD says He will pronounce His judgments "…because they have forsaken Me…" That's the reason He gives in verse 16. He adds that they burned incense to other gods and worshiped the works of their own hands.

The answer is intimidated. The LORD says, "Do not be intimidated by them, or I will terrify you before them." (Jeremiah 1:17). Right before that, Jeremiah is told to get ready, stand up and tell them everything the LORD commands.

The answer is the whole land and its leaders. The LORD says it's "…against the whole land…" and then He lists them: the kings of Judah, its officials, its priests, and the people of the land. That's a long list to stand against. The LORD says He has made Jeremiah like a fortified city, an iron pillar, and bronze walls.

The answer is False. The LORD says, "They will fight against you but will never overcome you, since I am with you to deliver you…" The fighting happens. The promise is that Jeremiah won't be overcome.
